official_measurement_examples.name: Seek-to-further duty
official_measurement_examples.fact: Protected Landscapes duty guidance explains that relevant authorities must now seek to further statutory purposes rather than merely have regard to them.

official_measurement_examples.name: Setting beyond boundary
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance states the Protected Landscapes duty can be relevant to functions or development outside a National Park or National Landscape boundary where the setting or purposes may be affected.

official_measurement_examples.name: National Landscape terminology
official_measurement_examples.fact: Defra guidance uses National Landscape as the rebranded name for AONB while noting that the name change itself is not statutory.

official_measurement_examples.name: Management plan role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Protected Landscape management plans are statutory management documents and provide strategic context, but planning guidance states they do not themselves form the statutory development plan.

official_measurement_examples.name: National Park boundary data
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's July 2026 National Parks dataset maps designation boundaries and purposes; boundary membership alone does not determine a proposal outcome.

official_measurement_examples.name: AONB dataset timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's AONB dataset remains the statutory-designation geography even though public-facing terminology commonly uses National Landscape.

official_measurement_examples.name: National Character Area distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: National Character Areas are broad landscape-character units used for planning and management strategy and are not equivalent to statutory National Park or AONB designations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Policy separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Protected Landscape designation, setting, management plans, NPPF policy tests and planning permission remain separate considerations and cannot be collapsed into a binary parcel clearance score.

core_rules: Protected Landscape boundary membership is not automatic planning refusal
land outside a Protected Landscape can still affect its setting or statutory purposes
National Landscape branding must not be confused with the statutory AONB designation term
management plans provide strategic context but are not themselves planning permission
management plan objectives must retain their plan period and local scope
National Character Areas are landscape-character evidence not statutory designation boundaries
Natural England designation geometry does not determine ownership or access rights
NPPF policy weight must be applied to the specific proposal rather than inferred from proximity alone
major-development policy tests must not be assumed satisfied or failed without proposal evidence
Protected Landscapes Targets and Outcomes Framework targets are not parcel development quotas
historic boundary versions must not silently override newer authoritative revisions
landscape visual effects require proposal-specific assessment and cannot be inferred from designation alone
Protected Landscape compliance does not reserve infrastructure capacity
designation evidence does not replace heritage ecology flood or other independent controls
no parcel landscape clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
